1.explanation: The core of the problem lives in the `UpdateLabelHandler` module, specifically in the `ensureInternalLabelDi` helper. When text is removed (`!text && di.label`), the code sets `di.label = null` instead of deleting the property. This leaves an empty `label` key on the DI, which downstream code sees and tries to process, causing lint errors. Adjusting or replacing this assignment to remove the property entirely (e.g. `delete di.label`) will prevent the null placeholder from persisting.
1.bug_scenario: When the user clears the label of a BPMN Task (i.e. deletes the text completely), the underlying DI (diagram interchange) entry for that element still retains a `label` property set to `null`. In the screenshot/video, when the label text is removed, you can see in the developer console that `di.label` still exists (with value `null`) instead of being removed entirely, which then causes downstream tools (such as BPMN linting integrations) to error out.

2.explanation: The core of the issue lies in the `ensureInternalLabelDi` helper within `UpdateLabelHandler`. When the new text is empty, the code sets `di.label = null` rather than deleting the property altogether. As a result, `di.label` continues to exist (albeit null), causing lint and validation tools to treat it as an unexpected attribute. Fixing this requires updating `ensureInternalLabelDi` so that on empty text it removes the `label` field (e.g. `delete di.label`) instead of assigning `null`. This change ensures `di.label` truly does not exist after clearing the label.
2.bug_scenario: In the provided animation the user removes the text label from a BPMN Task. Visually the label disappears as expected, but the underlying DI (diagram interchange) element still retains a `label` property set to `null`. This residual `null` property triggers linting errors and other downstream tool failures because `di.label` should be fully removed rather than left as `null`.
